inputs.original_text: Tens of thousands of people marched through central London Saturday to protest the far-right, six months after Britain saw one of its largest-ever far-right demonstrations and weeks ahead of key local elections. Organised by hundreds of groups, including trade unions, anti-racism campaigners and Muslim representative bodies, the Together Alliance event was billed as the biggest [...] The post Protesters rally in London against UK far-right rise appeared first on Digital Journal .
inputs.modified_text:
Look at what we are dealing with on our streets. Just look at the radical left and their institutional allies marching through central London this Saturday. Tens of thousands turned out, whipped into a frenzy by groups like the Together Alliance, trade unions, and various activist bodies, all under the guise of pushing back against what they hystericaly call a surge of extremism. 

Let's call this what it really is: a coordinated attempt by progressive agitators to bully the public and intimidate ordinary citizens just weeks ahead of key local elections. They want to muzzle traditional values and silence anyone who dares to question their open-borders agenda, all while propping up a narrative that Britain is fundamentally hateful. It’s entirely predictable—just six months after one of the largest-ever demonstrations Britain saw, the establishment and their union backers are desperate to sweep real concerns about national identity and social order under the rug. Instead of promoting personal responsibility and community stability, these activists demand radical institutional reform and division. They use buzzwords like solidarity to tear down our heritage, but millions of Britons see right through it.
